name: Terma
desc: Danish defence and aerospace group making radars, self-protection systems, aerostructures and space equipment for military customers.
capacity_detail: Revenue DKK 2.883bn in financial year 2024/25 (Terma Annual Report 2024/25, per Wikipedia)
markets: Defence and aerospace customers in Denmark and abroad; about 2,000-2,200 staff worldwide; owned by Thrige Holding A/S.
rationale: Rising European defence budgets and F35 supply-chain role give Terma reason to raise its profile with governments and engineering talent.

name: WB Group
desc: Polish defence group making loitering munitions, military drones, battlefield communications and fire-control systems such as Warmate and FlyEye.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 0.4bn in 2023 (Wikipedia infobox); Polish Development Fund holds a 24% minority stake bought in 2017
markets: Polish armed forces and export customers for drones, loitering munitions and command-and-control systems.
rationale: Fast-growing European drone maker courting export buyers and engineers; F1 hospitality offers access to defence and government decision makers.

name: Havelsan
desc: Turkish defence software and systems company building command-and-control, simulation, training and cyber-security solutions for armed forces.
ownership: state fund: Turkish Armed Forces Foundation
capacity_detail: Net sales from production TRY 18.75bn in 2025, ISO 500 rank 135 (about USD 470M at roughly 40 TRY per USD)
markets: Turkish armed forces and government, with defence export ambitions; 98% owned by the Turkish Armed Forces Strengthening Foundation.
rationale: Turkey's defence exporters are building international brands; the Istanbul Grand Prix's return would give Havelsan a home showcase.

name: Togg
desc: Turkish electric car maker producing the T10X and T10F models at its Gemlik factory and running the Trugo charging network.
capacity_detail: Revenue TRY 65bn in 2025 (Turkish Wikipedia infobox); 39,020 cars sold in 2025
markets: Turkey, with Trugo charging stations in all 81 provinces and a stated goal of exporting to European countries.
rationale: National EV brand seeking European exports needs international credibility; F1 and a Turkish Grand Prix return offer a global showcase.

name: SENER
desc: Spanish family-owned engineering and technology group working in mobility, aerospace and defence, energy and data-centre design.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 933M in 2025, up 31.4%, order book EUR 1.912bn
markets: International markets give 88% of sales, growing in Canada, Australia, the United States and Central Europe, especially Germany.
rationale: Engineering group winning space, defence and data-centre work worldwide; F1's engineering image suits recruitment and client hospitality.

name: Be8
desc: Brazilian biofuels company producing biodiesel and ethanol and developing green hydrogen and biogenic CO2 capture projects.
capacity_detail: Net revenue BRL 10bn in 2025, up 36%; EBITDA BRL 809M
markets: Brazil, with plants in Rio Grande do Sul and Paraná and acquisitions in the North, Northeast and Centre-West regions.
rationale: Biofuel producer promoting low-carbon fuels; F1's 2026 sustainable-fuel rules and the São Paulo Grand Prix make a natural platform.

name: Inpasa
desc: Corn ethanol producer with plants in Brazil and Paraguay, also making DDGS animal feed and corn oil.
capacity_detail: Net revenue BRL 22.8bn and net profit BRL 4.9bn for the Inpasa Group (2025 Sustainability Report)
markets: Production units in Brazil and Paraguay; products reach 40 countries on five continents.
rationale: Largest corn-ethanol maker promoting renewable fuels; F1's sustainable-fuel shift and Brazilian Grand Prix suit a brand-building push.

name: FS Bioenergia
desc: Brazilian producer of corn ethanol, animal-feed DDGs and bioenergy from three plants in Mato Grosso.
capacity_detail: Net revenue BRL 12,965.9M in fiscal 2026 (April 2025 to March 2026), FS earnings release
markets: Brazil, with three corn-ethanol plants in Mato Grosso and one under construction; owned by Summit (43.2%) and Amaggi (40%).
rationale: Carbon-negative ethanol pitch fits F1's sustainable-fuel era; São Paulo Grand Prix gives a home-market stage.

name: Atvos
desc: Brazilian sugarcane bioenergy company producing ethanol, sugar and electricity from eight agro-industrial units.
capacity_detail: Net revenue BRL 7.7bn in the 2024/2025 crop year; Mubadala-affiliated fund is reference shareholder
markets: Brazil, with eight agro-industrial units able to crush 38 million tonnes of sugarcane and more than 11,000 employees.
rationale: Mubadala-backed ethanol producer could use F1's sustainable-fuel narrative and Abu Dhabi links to build its renewable-fuel brand.

name: JetBrains
desc: Software developer tools company making IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and other IDEs, the Kotlin language and AI coding agents.
capacity_detail: Revenue CZK 16,008M (about USD 731M) in 2025 for JetBrains s.r.o., per its filed Czech accounts
markets: Developers worldwide; most active customer countries include the US, China, Germany, India, UK, France, Brazil, Korea, Poland and Canada.
rationale: Developer-tools rivals and AI coding firms already sponsor F1 teams; JetBrains could reach engineers and enterprise buyers globally.

name: Lionbridge
desc: Language services company providing translation, localisation, content and AI training-data services to global enterprises.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 546M in 2024, ranked sixth in the 2025 Nimdzi 100
markets: Enterprise clients worldwide with operations in more than 26 countries.
rationale: Multilingual content for global brands mirrors F1's worldwide audience; hospitality would help Lionbridge win enterprise localisation and AI-data contracts.

name: Colt Technology Services
desc: Network services company providing high-bandwidth fibre connectivity, voice and data-centre services to enterprises and carriers.
capacity_detail: Group consolidated turnover exceeded EUR 750M in each of the last two fiscal years (Colt country-by-country tax report, FY2025)
markets: Enterprise and carrier customers across Europe, the United States and Asia.
rationale: F1's data-hungry race operations showcase low-latency networks; telecom rivals already sponsor teams, giving Colt a B2B hospitality platform.
theme: AI infrastructure: data centres & GPU cloud

name: SubCom
desc: US supplier of turnkey subsea fibre-optic cable systems, covering engineering, manufacturing, marine installation and maintenance.
capacity_detail: Cerberus closed a single-asset continuation vehicle for SubCom with about USD 2.3bn of commitments, led by CVC, in April 2026
markets: Subsea cable systems for telecom carriers and cloud providers worldwide.

signals.raise: Cerberus continuation vehicle with about USD 2.3bn of commitments (Apr 2026; https://cvc.com/media/news/2026/cerberus-closes-23-billion-single-asset-continuation-vehicle-for-subcom/)

rationale: AI-driven cable demand brings hyperscaler buyers; F1 hospitality offers access to cloud and telecom decision makers worldwide.
theme: AI infrastructure: data centres & GPU cloud

name: GlobalConnect
industry: Nordic fibre network and data centres
desc: Nordic digital infrastructure company running a fibre network of over 250,000 km plus colocation data centres.
capacity_detail: Revenue and other income SEK 8.0bn in 2025 (SEK 8.1bn in 2024); adjusted EBITDA SEK 4.8bn
markets: Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Germany and Finland, serving business, carrier and data-centre customers.

signals.marketing: New CEO Lasse Pilgaard to succeed Martin Lippert in Sep 2026 (https://www.mynewsdesk.com/globalconnect/pressreleases/ceo-of-globalconnect-to-step-down-in-september-lasse-pilgaard-to-succeed-martin-lippert-3446394)

rationale: Nordic fibre backbone courting hyperscalers and AI data-centre builders could use F1 hospitality for B2B relationship building.
theme: AI infrastructure: data centres & GPU cloud

name: Yotta Data Services
desc: Indian data-centre and sovereign AI cloud provider offering colocation, managed services and GPU computing to enterprises.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 150M at a USD 3.9bn valuation in 2026; plans an Indian IPO of up to USD 1.5bn by March 2027
markets: India-based data centres and GPU cloud; international customers make up 75-80% of its customer base.

signals.raise: USD 150M from non-institutional investors at USD 3.9bn valuation (2026; https://inc42.com/buzz/ai-infra-provider-yotta-eyes-1-5-bn-ipo-by-march-2027-report/)
signals.ipo: Plans to file draft IPO papers with SEBI in Oct 2026 for a listing by March 2027 (Sep 2026; https://inc42.com/buzz/ai-infra-provider-yotta-eyes-1-5-bn-ipo-by-march-2027-report/)

rationale: Pre-IPO AI cloud provider courting global customers; GPU-cloud rivals already sponsor F1 teams, offering visibility before listing.
theme: AI infrastructure: data centres & GPU cloud

name: GalaxySpace
desc: Chinese commercial space company building low-Earth-orbit broadband communication satellites and satellite internet systems.
capacity_detail: Post-money valuation about CNY 32bn after its latest round (eight rounds in total), reported 2026
markets: China, building satellite internet and LEO communication constellations.

signals.ipo: Filed for IPO tutoring with CSRC, aiming at the STAR Market (Mar 2026; https://sohu.com/a/1005445459_100085330)

rationale: Pre-IPO satellite-internet firm building a national brand; F1's Shanghai race offers visibility with investors and government buyers.

name: RUAG
desc: Swiss federal defence company maintaining, upgrading and supporting military aircraft, vehicles and systems for the Swiss Armed Forces.
capacity_detail: RUAG MRO net sales CHF 824.6M in 2025 (CHF 775M in 2024), per the Federal Council release
markets: Mainly the Swiss Armed Forces and Swiss federal government, with aviation maintenance customers in Switzerland and abroad.
rationale: State-owned defence supplier with limited consumer need; F1 could help recruiting engineers but government ownership restricts marketing spend.

name: HOUMO.AI
desc: Chinese chip designer making compute-in-memory and edge large-model AI chips such as the M50 and A20.
capacity_detail: Completed a Series B of several billion yuan (数十亿元人民币, at least about USD 280M), reported Nov 2026
markets: China, with over 150 product design wins and more than 100 customers for its edge AI chips.

signals.raise: Series B of several billion yuan from industrial, state and international investors (Nov 2026; https://finance.sina.cn/stock/jdts/2026-11-04/detail-inixpvuw9446551.d.html)

rationale: Newly funded AI-chip challenger building a brand among device makers; chip rivals already sponsor F1, though focus is domestic.
